doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

title: Visual art: cover art, acrylics, and uncle's crayons
summary: He did cover art for Lester Bowie's Numbers One and Two, now paints in acrylics, and John Corbett found his earlier paintings; Rowe links this to his uncle's crayon art.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Let me ask you about your visual art, which — didn’t you have the cover art on Lester’s thing that you just mentioned?
Yeah, yeah. Lester Bowie’s Numbers One and Two” yes. It was at the opening in Chicago.
What is the medium that you work in?

Well I had some crossover things from when I was doing oils so I finished those up, but I’m doing acrylics now. Because I don’t want to breathe all of the oils and all this kind of thing like that anymore. So yeah I’m using acrylics and I use a brush and then also I use these pens you know, because they’re almost like drawing. Yeah, yeah. So that’s what I’m doing. But of course but John Corbett went back and found, looked under every rock and stone and found every painting that I darn near ever did in my life. You know John Corbett is a man that doesn’t have the word no in his vocabulary.
Well it’s a nice, sort of continuing the circle that perhaps your uncle started with his crayons.
